Hannah,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Procurement reviewed your standard MSA and asked us to confirm Greenfield Medical will be covered for personal injury and property damage arising from use of the service. Their standard clause asks for an explicit carve-out to the limitation of liability for bodily injury and physical property damage (they typically include a clause that these are uncapped / not subject to the general liability cap). I attached the procurement template so you can see their exact language.

Can you let me know whether Redwood can accept that carve-out or propose an alternative? We need a redline for our procurement team by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Sara

Karthik / Laura — looping you in for legal + contract ops input.

Sara, thanks for the heads up and for the template. High level: our standard LOL (limitation of liability) caps are a key part of our risk model. We generally keep bodily injury/property damage exceptions extremely narrow for SaaS — Greenfield's ask for an uncapped exemption is unusual for software-only services.

Can you confirm two things for us so we can advise faster:
- Any on-prem hardware or installation Redwood would perform at Greenfield sites? (Greenfield operations seem cloud-first but check)
- Is procurement requesting that the carve-out apply even when alleged harm is caused by Customer configuration or third-party integrations?

Planning: Karthik, can you suggest fallback language that preserves our cap but addresses a hospital's concern about physical harm tied directly to our on-site equipment or installation? Laura — if we can accept anything narrower, we need a short form redline to return to Sara by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@greenfieldmed.com>, procurement@greenfieldmed.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:47:30 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — personal injury & property coverage request

Hannah / Laura / Sara — quick legal POV and proposed redline (high level):

1) Baseline stance: For cloud-hosted SaaS with no physical installation, we decline uncapped bodily injury/property damage carve-outs. Our commercial insurance covers certain risks; accepting unlimited exposure is not acceptable.

2) Narrow acceptable carve-out: We can consider a limited exception where Redwood (a) supplies physical hardware or performs on-site installation and (b) our direct negligent acts or omissions cause verifiable physical injury or property damage. Even then, the exception should be "subject to insurance limits" (i.e., up to the limits of our commercial general liability and umbrella policies) and should not expand to cover third-party integrations or Customer negligence.

3) Suggested redline language (plain text):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing limitation of liability, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, indirect or punitive damages. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitation of liability shall not apply to direct damages arising from bodily injury or physical damage to real property caused by Redwood’s willful misconduct or gross negligence in performing on-site installation of Redwood-owned hardware. Any liability for such bodily injury or physical property damage shall in all cases be limited to the greater of (a) the amounts recoverable under Redwood’s applicable commercial general liability and umbrella insurance policies in effect at the time of the claim, or (b) the amount set forth in the applicable order form, if higher."

Practical notes:
- This keeps the carve-out narrow (on-site hardware + our gross negligence/willful misconduct) and ties exposure to insurance—consistent with enterprise procurement expectations.
- We should also request indemnities from Customer if Customer-supplied hardware or changes contributed to the harm.

Laura — can you convert this into a tracked redline (docx) and include a fallback that offers a higher insurance dollar figure if Greenfield needs a specific cap number? I recommend offering to provide liability insurance certificates and confirming policy limits.

Karthik
General Counsel (interim)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_proposal_Greenfield.docx

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — personal injury & property coverage request

Hi Sara — attached is our proposed redline and a short cover note. Changes summary:
- We decline an uncapped carve-out.
- We offer a narrow exception limited to bodily injury/physical damage caused by Redwood’s on-site hardware installation where Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct is the proximate cause.
- Any recovery under that exception is capped at our commercial insurance limits (we included options to list a specific dollar cap if you prefer).
- We added a clause excluding harm caused primarily by Customer configuration, Customer-supplied hardware, or third-party integrations.

If Greenfield needs an explicit numeric cap (rather than insurance-limited), we can propose a dollar figure for an additional fee or escalate to executive approval — please indicate which route procurement prefers.

Next steps: if this looks acceptable, Hannah will confirm and we’ll exchange insurance certificates. If Greenfield insists on an uncapped carve-out, we will need to escalate to Sarah (VP Sales) + Legal risk committee for approval.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
